correctness.rationale: Terminal EF1 cardinality reduction to (2,1,1) and rank condition is proved; backward recursion explicitly alternates adversarial valuation vectors then allocator decisions, and two independent exact full-game checkers embedded at verification/verify_game.py and verification/verify_numeric.cpp both confirm all four game values, including n=3,m=4 3-tier unrestricted allocator win and 4-tier loss. Infinite positive real magnitudes transfer by strict ordinal invariance, not by experiments alone.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary full-text sections and published mathematical records were compared by theorem implications. A known 2025 ternary impossibility assumes EF1 at every time, whereas the new positive guarantee concerns only terminal EF1; the 2026 paper gives approximate three-agent results and an at-least-five-agent exactness obstruction. Previous two-agent/three-good cutoff does not imply the three-agent four-good game values. No direct or stronger exact covering result found, with residual unindexed-literature risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible independent finite-game classification may exist.
The method establishes existence via a finite backward-induction policy rather than an efficient closed-form allocation rule.
The exact ordinal reduction is special to three agents and four strictly positive goods; extending it uncritically would be invalid.

value.rationale: The exact positive/negative threshold for a canonical smallest-surplus three-agent terminal-EF1 market identifies when ternary personalized preferences can still be served fairly without future information. Neither a fixed same-recipient nor a fixed distinct-recipient first-two pattern works, yielding a substantive necessary temporary fairness violation for any eventual-EF1 policy, and clarifying the difference from temporal impossibility results.
